items.name: Communication.FEAT_SupportForTimeBasedArchitecture
items.text: The communication framework shall provide API to support a time-based architecture.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_SupportForDataDrivenArchitecture
items.text: The communication framework shall provide API to support a data-driven architecture.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_SupportForRequestDrivenArchitecture
items.text: The communication framework shall provide API to support a request-driven architecture.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_CommunicationInterfaces
items.text: A communication interface consists of a combination of any number of the following elements: Event-Types, Methods, Signals.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_EventType
items.text: An event-type is part of a communication interface and has a name and a data type. The producer can assign a value to it. Consumers can subscribe to value-changed events of the element or poll unseen, cached events.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_Method
items.text: A method is part of a communication interface and has a name, a specified application routine with a given set of parameters and a return type. When a communication partner issues a call to the method with the required parameters, it shall invoke the application routine with the provided parameters, and return its result to the communication partner. A method call shall be possible both synchronously and asynchronously.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_Field
items.text: A field is a component of a communication interface and is defined by a name and a data type, along with dedicated getter and setter methods. The producer has the ability to assign a value to the field. Consumers can either subscribe to receive notifications when the field’s value changes or poll the cached values of fields that have not yet been seen. Additionally, consumers can retrieve the current value of the field using the getter method or update the field’s value through the setter method.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_Signal
items.text: A signal is part of a communication interface and has a name. A client can trigger the signal. The service instance offering the trigger can wait for the signal to be triggered or check if the signal was triggered. Signals can not transport data.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_ProducerConsumerPattern
items.text: Communication shall be cached based on the producer-consumer pattern.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_ServiceInstance
items.text: Multiple service instances shall be able to offer the same interface.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_ServiceInstanceNames
items.text: A service instance is offered under one or more unique names by which it can be discovered. Names follow a POSIX path style.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_Versioning
items.text: The communication framework shall support versioning of service instances. Version information of a service instance is binding-specific.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_ServiceLocationTransparency
items.text: The interface to access service instances is agnostic to the binding used to communicate with the service.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_StatelessCommunication
items.text: The communication framework shall support stateless communication.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_ServiceInstanceGranularity
items.text: The communication framework shall support multiple service instances per software architecture element.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_ServiceDiscovery
items.text: The communication framework shall provide service discovery to find available services during runtime. Service discovery shall consider version compatibility.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_SafeCommunication
items.text: The communication framework shall support safe communication involving communication partners on the same or multiple criticality levels.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_DataCorruption
items.text: Consumers with lower criticality shall not be able to corrupt data consumed by partners with higher criticality.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_DataReordering
items.text: Consumers with lower criticality shall not be able to modify the order of data consumed by partners with higher criticality.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_DataRepetition
items.text: Consumers with lower criticality shall not be able to duplicate data consumed by other communication partners with higher criticality.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_DataLoss
items.text: Consumers with lower criticality shall not be able to drop data before it is consumed by partners with higher criticality.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_ZeroCopy
items.text: The communication framework shall enable Zero-Copy communication without copying to-be-transferred data.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_SupportForMultipleProgrammingLanguages
items.text: The communication framework shall provide a public API for each supported programming language of S-CORE.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_SupportForProgrammingLanguageIdioms
items.text: Each public API shall support the idioms of the programming language it is written in.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_UseProgrammingLanguageInfrastructure
items.text: Each public API shall use core infrastructure of its programming language and accompanying standard libraries, whenever possible and meaningful.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_FullyMockablePublicAPI
items.text: The public API shall be fully mockable.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_FakeBinding
items.text: The communication framework shall provide a fake binding.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_MultiBindingSupport
items.text: The communication framework shall support multiple bindings.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_BindingAgnosticPublicAPI
items.text: The public API of the communication framework shall be binding-agnostic.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_MultiBindingDeploymentConfiguration
items.text: The association of a service instance and the appropriate binding shall be specified in the deployment configuration.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_DeploymentConfigurationAtRuntime
items.text: Deployment configuration shall be read from an integrity-checked configuration file at runtime.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_SupportForTracing
items.text: The communication framework shall provide infrastructure to enable binding-agnostic, zero-copy, read-only tracing of communication.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_AccessControlListPlacement
items.text: The communication framework shall support an Access Control Lists in the deployment configuration.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_AccessControlListPerServiceInstance
items.text: The communication framework shall support an Access Control List per service instance.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_AccessControlListForProducer
items.text: The communication framework shall support an Access Control List for the communication partner offering a service instance (producer).

items.name: Communication.FEAT_AccessControlListForConsumer
items.text: The communication framework shall support an Access Control List for the communication partner consuming a service instance.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_CommunicationASILLevel
items.text: The communication framework shall support safe communication up to ASIL-B.

items.name: Communication.FEAT_ErrorHandling
items.text:
(C++) exceptions shall not be used for error handling.
The best way to deal with errors is to try to resolve those component internally. If not possible the caller of the function shall be notified of the error.
For (error) returns there is a specific library to be used in S-CORE, it is the Score::Result library which is part of
the Base Libraries feature.

items.name: Communication.ASR_ErrorHandling
items.text:
(C++) exceptions shall not be used for error handling.
The best way to deal with errors is to try to resolve those component internally. If not possible the caller of the function shall be notified of the error.
For (error) returns there is a specific library to be used in S-CORE, it is the score::Result library which is part of
the Base Libraries feature.

items.name: Communication.ASR_InterProcessCommunication
items.text: The platform shall support inter-process communication.

items.name: Communication.ASR_IntraProcessCommunication
items.text: The platform shall support intra-process communication.

items.name: Communication.ASR_ExtensibleExternalCommunication
items.text: The platform shall support external communication via well established protocols e.g. Zenoh, DDS, SOME/IP.

items.name: Communication.ASR_SafeCommunication
items.text: The platform shall support safe communication in terms of ISO 26262. I.e. it shall provide mechanisms to avoid communication errors defined by the ISO 26262.

items.name: Communication.ASR_SecureCommunication
items.text: The information exchanged between applications shall be protected against unauthorized access and manipulation. The platform shall provide mechanisms to ensure confidentiality, integrity, and authenticity of the exchanged information.

items.name: Communication.ASR_SupportForTimeBasedArchitectures
items.text: The platform shall support a deterministic, time-based application execution model that triggers logic based on predefined schedules or polling intervals.

items.name: Communication.ASR_SupportForDataDrivenArchitecture
items.text: The platform shall support an event-driven, high-throughput application architecture where execution is triggered by data changes.

items.name: Communication.ASR_SupportForRequestDrivenArchitecture
items.text: The platform shall support a request-driven application architecture that processes requests on-demand.

items.name: Communication.ASR_ProgrammingLanguagesForApplicationDevelopment
items.text: The platform shall support implementation of applications in the following programming languages up to the highest ASIL level as defined in automotive_safety: C++, Rust.

items.name: Communication.ASR_TracingOfCommunication
items.text: The platform shall support the tracing of communication events for internal and external communication systems.

items.name: Communication.ASR_AvailabilityOfCommunicationPartners
items.text: The platform shall provide a mechanism to detect the availability of communication partners for internal and external communication systems and provide the required information to communicate with them.

items.name: Communication.ASR_StablePublicApi
items.text: The platform shall provide a stable API for the communication middleware.

items.name: Communication.CreationOfSkeletonNotPossible
items.text: It is not possible to create a skeleton instance

items.name: Communication.ServiceOfferedWithoutInitialFieldValue
items.text: A service is offered, although at least one of its field has no initial value set by the provider.

items.name: Communication.ServiceNotOffered
items.text: A skeleton service is offering a service, but the service is silently not offered. Note: offered in this case means, that it is also connectable

items.name: Communication.ServiceOfferedOnWrongBinding
items.text: A skeleton is offering a service on the wrong binding. Meaning, the service is not offered on the intended binding, but on an unintended one.

items.name: Communication.ServiceOfferedUnderWrongIds
items.text: A skeleton is offering a service with wrong identifiers. This can include a service id, a instance id or also the service version.

items.name: Communication.OffersAlreadyOfferedService
items.text: A skeleton offers a service that was already offered. Either by another process or by itself.

items.name: Communication.ServiceOnlyPartiallyOffered
items.text: A skeleton offers a service, which is not visible to all consumers, but only to parts of them.

items.name: Communication.StopOfferNotStoppedInSD
items.text: A service instance was offered via service discovery, but it wasn't withdrawn from service discovery in the stop offer.

items.name: Communication.StopOfferWrongInstanceStoppedInSD
items.text: Same as in StopOfferNotStoppedInSD. Additionally another service instance, which is still being offered, is withdrawn from service discovery.

items.name: Communication.StopOfferUnlinkWrongSHMObjects
items.text: Skeleton instance did unlink shared memory objects which do not belong to the service instance being stop offered.

items.name: Communication.StopOfferInconsistent
items.text: Skeleton instance is in an inconsistent state after stop offering: Either the stop offer was not forwarded to the binding or failed at the binding. Or it wasn't forwarded to the dependent service elements or their bindings or failed at them.

items.name: Communication.MemoryAllocatedInWrongSection
items.text: The memory for an event is allocated in the wrong memory section (e.g. in Heap, another Shared Memory segment or the stack).

items.name: Communication.TooFewMemoryAllocated
items.text: The event allocation allocates too few memory (including no memory at all).

items.name: Communication.WronglyAlignedMemoryAllocated
items.text: The memory for an event/field is allocated in a wrongly aligned manner.

items.name: Communication.TooMuchMemoryAllocated
items.text: There is too much memory allocated for one event/field

items.name: Communication.AllocatesAlreadyAllocatedMemory
items.text: The memory for an event/field is allocated from already allocated memory (not free memory).

items.name: Communication.SendingEventChangesUserData
items.text: A call to send manipulates the data that was provided by the caller.

items.name: Communication.SendingAnEventOrFieldSendsDataOnlyPartially
items.text: Data that is send by the user, only reaches partially the consumer. This can happen in two ways, only a partial number of consumers see the data or all consumers see only partial data.

items.name: Communication.SendingEventOnlyPartiallyNotifiesConsumer
items.text: When data is sent, consumers that have a callback registered, are only partially notified.

items.name: Communication.SendingEventSendsToWrongConsumer
items.text: An event or field is sent to the wrong consumer.

items.name: Communication.SendingAnEventOrFieldSendsSameSampleNtimes
items.text: Instead of sending a sample (one data point) only once, it is send multiple times.

items.name: Communication.SendingEventDoesNotFreeResources
items.text: Resources in the middleware that have been allocated with a previous allocation, are not freed after returning from send/update.

items.name: Communication.WrongResourcesFreed
items.text: A destruction of one skeleton instances, frees the resources of another skeleton instance.

items.name: Communication.NoResourcesFreed
items.text: The resources allocated on construction and during operation are not freed on destruction.

items.name: Communication.EarlyCleanUp
items.text: Resources are freed while still being used.

items.name: Communication.WrongMethodInArgsUsed
items.text: Unintended input arguments are used in a service method call. Therefore, the method call gets executed with wrong input data.

items.name: Communication.WrongMethodCalled
items.text: Either the wrong user provided method handler is called or no user handler is called at all. Therefore, the method call results are invalid/garbage.

items.name: Communication.WrongResultsProvided
items.text: The result of a method call is either not provided in the expected location, leaving uninitialized data in the expected location or it is provided in an inconsistent state. Therefore, the method call results are invalid/garbage.

items.name: Communication.StartFindServiceCallbackCalledUnexpectedly
items.text: The user-provided callback is invoked, even though it should not be invoked.

items.name: Communication.ServiceNotFound
items.text: A proxy does not find a service instance, even though it was offered by a skeleton.

items.name: Communication.WrongServiceFound
items.text: A proxy instance finds a wrong service. This could be either a wrong service instance or a completely wrong service.

items.name: Communication.ServiceIsFoundButDoesNotExist
items.text: Finding a service, returns a service, even though no service instance was offered.

items.name: Communication.StartedFindServiceIsNotStopped
items.text: A user called "StartFindService" with a given handler, and since "StopFindService" does not work, services can still be found.

items.name: Communication.WrongStartfindserviceIsStopped
items.text: The handle provided to StopFindService, is identified as another one and thus stops the wrong service discovery query.

items.name: Communication.SubscribeToWrongEvent
items.text: A service proxy subscribes to a wrong event. This either means that this event does not exist at all, is offered by another service instance, another event in the current instance or a completely different service.

items.name: Communication.SubscribeWithWrongMaxSampleCount
items.text: A proxy instance subscribes to an event to with a wrong sample count, meaning a different one that was provided by the user.

items.name: Communication.DoesNotSubscribe
items.text: A proxy does not subscribe to a skeleton. Thus, a skeleton does not know that a proxy is interested in data.

items.name: Communication.ReceiveHandlerNotInvoked
items.text: A proxy has set a receive handler and a skeleton is updating an event, but the receive handler is never invoked.

items.name: Communication.ReceiveHandlerInvokedWithWrongEvent
items.text: A receive handler registered for an event, gets called because of an update of an different event.

items.name: Communication.ReceiveHandlerInvokedMultipleTimes
items.text: A receive handler is invoked multiple times, even though only one event update happend.

items.name: Communication.ReceiveHandlerInvokedWithoutEventNotification
items.text: A receive handler is invoked, even though no event update happend.

items.name: Communication.CallbackNotInvokedDespiteSamplesAvailable
items.text: GetNewSamples() gets called on an event with a callback F, but the callback gets called not at all, although at least one new sample is available.

items.name: Communication.CallbackInvokedWithWrongData
items.text: A proxy receives a sample pointer via callback F(), but the data does not contain the expected one.

items.name: Communication.UsesToManySampleptr
items.text: User is already max. sample count SamplePtr, but we are still handing out SamplePtrs in callback F().

items.name: Communication.ReturnsWrongSampleCount
items.text: Value returned by GetNewSample() does not match with the number of calls to callback F().

items.name: Communication.SucceedsDespiteAnError
items.text: A user calls GetNewSamples() on a proxy instance and receives a sample count, even though he should have received an error.

items.name: Communication.ReturnsWrongFreeSampleCount
items.text: A user has already M SamplePtr in use from a max. announced number N, but GetFreeSampleCount() returns a different value than N-M.

items.name: Communication.DoesNotUnsubscribe
items.text: A proxy is subscribed to an event, tries to unsubscribe, but silently fails to unsubscribe.

items.name: Communication.UnsubscribesFromWrongEvent
items.text: A user unsubscribes from an event, but the unsubscribe is silently carried out on another event.

items.name: Communication.DoesNotImplicitRemoveReceiveHandler
items.text: A proxy has registered a receive handler and unsubscribes, this should lead to the case that a receive handler is no longer called. In this failure mode, the receive handler would still be called.

items.name: Communication.MapContainingNonexistentEvents
items.text: The map that is visible to the user, contains events that are not actually existing (e.g. in the configuration).

items.name: Communication.IncompleteMapOfEvents
items.text: The user gets presented not all events the generic proxy supports.

items.name: Communication.TheSizeReturnedIsBiggerThenTheActualValue
items.text: The user receives a size, that is bigger then the actual value.

items.name: Communication.TheSizeReturnedIsSmallerThenTheActualSize
items.text: The user receives a size, that is smaller then the actual value.

items.name: Communication.WrongIndicationIfFormatIsSerialized
items.text: A user, using HasSerializedFormat(), receives the wrong value.

items.name: Communication.MethodCallBlocksLongerThanExpected
items.text: A call to a service-method on the client/consumer side blocks longer than expected (or indefinite). This is a specific instance of FailureMode [AnyFunctionBlocksLongerThanExpected], but since with service-methods we have concrete root causes in the form of message-passing behaviour and behaviour of user-provided handler, we have this specific failure mode.

items.name: Communication.WrongMethodInArgsProvided
items.text: Unintended input arguments are provided to a service method call. Therefore, the method call gets executed with wrong input data.

items.name: Communication.WrongReturnValueUsed
items.text: Unintended results are provided from a service method call. Therefore, the caller of the method works on wrong data.

items.name: Communication.DoesNotFreeResourcesOnDestruction
items.text: A SampleAllocateePtr or SamplePtr is destroyed, which should lead to a freeing of resources, but caused by a fault they are not freed.

items.name: Communication.FreesWrongResources
items.text: A SampleAllocateePtr or SamplePtr free the wrong resources associated with them.

items.name: Communication.DoesNotReserveResources
items.text: A SamplePtr or SampleAllocateePtr do not increase their respective ref-counts and thus avoid data changes.

items.name: Communication.DoesNotUpdateFreeSampleCountCorrectly
items.text: When a SamplePtr gets created or destroyed for a given event instance, the Free Sample Count of this instance doesn't get updated accordingly

items.name: Communication.ReturnsWrongData
items.text: On dereferenciation of a SamplePtr or SampleAllocateePtr wrong data is returned.

items.name: Communication.MethodSignatureElementPtrWrongTarget
items.text: On de-referencing of a MethodSignatureElementPtr wrong data is returned.

items.name: Communication.MethodSignatureElementPtrFailsToFree
items.text: On destruction of a MethodSignatureElementPtr wrong memory is freed or not freed at all.

items.name: Communication.MonotonicSemiDynamicMemoryAllocation
items.text: It shall be ensured that enough memory is configured for shared memory instances, in order that LoLa can perform all necessary allocations (e.g. push-back on a Vector).

items.name: Communication.CorrectlyConfiguredMaximumNumberOfSubscriber
items.text: It shall be ensured that correct maximum number of subscriber is configured for each event for each service instance.

items.name: Communication.CorrectlyConfiguredMaximumNumberOfMaximumElementsPerSubscriber
items.text: It shall be ensured that correct maximum number of elements per subscriber is configured for each event for each service instance.

items.name: Communication.CorrectlyConfiguredAsilLevel
items.text: It shall be ensured that the ASIL Level on process level and per service instance is correctly configured.

items.name: Communication.OnlyLoLaSupportedTypes
items.text: It shall be ensured that only types that are supported by LoLa are transmitted.

items.name: Communication.NoApisFromImplementationNamespace
items.text: It shall be ensured that no API calls from the implementation namespace (e.g `impl`) are directly invoked or types from within are directly used.

items.name: Communication.NoGuaranteesForNotifications
items.text: It shall be ensured that a miss behavior of event notification will not harm a safety goal.

items.name: Communication.CheckingForPossibleMessageOverflow
items.text: It shall be ensured that a message overflow, which results in message loss will not harm a safety goal. If this is not possible, a check for message overflow and necessary actions need to be performed.

items.name: Communication.DifferentUserForAsilAndQmProcesses
items.text: It shall be ensured that processes with a different ASIL shall be executed within different user-ids.

items.name: Communication.ConfigOnASafeFilesystem
items.text: It shall be ensured that any configuration item that is read at runtime by LoLa is stored on a safety certified filesystem (according to the highest supported safety level).

items.name: Communication.NoStaticContextSupport
items.text: It shall be ensured that LoLa is not used within static context within C++.

items.name: Communication.NoGuaranteeInAvailabilityOfServices
items.text: It shall be ensured that no safety goal is harmed, because a service instance is not found.

items.name: Communication.NoNotificationOnTerminationOfProducer
items.text: It shall be ensured that termination (either gracefully or due to a malfunction) of a producer will not lead to a violation of a safety goal.

items.name: Communication.CheckForNullptrOnAllocate
items.text: It shall be checked if Allocate() on an event will return a nullptr. If a nullptr is returned, the system shall transition to safe state.

items.name: Communication.OneProducerOnlyOneAllocateePtr
items.text: It shall be ensured that at any time a producer instance per event only holds one AllocateePtr.

items.name: Communication.NoCopySendWhileHoldingAllocateePtr
items.text: It shall be ensured that Send(const& value) is not invoked while an AllocateePtr is held.

items.name: Communication.NoneReentrantMethodsPerEventInstance
items.text: It shall be ensured that any LoLa API that is bound to a specific event instance is not called in a reentrant manner.

items.name: Communication.SkeletonAliveWhileItsAllocateePtrBeingUsed
items.text: It shall be ensured that a Skeleton instance is still alive while any AllocateePtr returned by it is used.

items.name: Communication.EventSubscriptionActiveWhileHoldingSamplePtr
items.text: It shall be ensured that Unsubscribe() isn't called on a proxy event instance as long as any SamplePtr provided by it, is still held. Also the corresponding proxy instance shall be kept alive as on destruction it would implicitly call Unsubscribe().

items.name: Communication.NoneTerminatingCallbacks
items.text: It shall be ensured that any callback passed to LoLa for invocation is not throwing.

items.name: Communication.ValidCallbacksWhileProxyAlive
items.text: It shall be ensured that all callbacks passed towards LoLa are valid as long as the associated proxy is alive.

items.name: Communication.QualityOfDataIsDependentOnProducer
items.text: It shall be ensured that the necessary quality of data is produced by the respective skeleton process.

items.name: Communication.ValidityOfPointerOnLoLaPointer
items.text: It shall be ensured that no pointer, pointing to the memory of a SamplePtr or AllocateePtr is used once the SamplePtr or AllocateePtr are invalid.

items.name: Communication.LoLaMemoryOnlyAccessedThroughLoLa
items.text: It shall be ensured that no other code accesses the mapped memory managed by LoLa.

items.name: Communication.NoSharedMemoryAllocationInNamespaceLola
items.text: It shall be ensured that no other code creates shared memory segments beginning with "lola".

items.name: Communication.OnlyQnx71Supported
items.text: It shall be ensured that any application containing LoLa is only executed on QNX Safe Operating System 7.1.

items.name: Communication.LoLaSpecificQnxMessagingEndPointsOnlyAccessedThroughLoLa
items.text: It shall be ensured that the LoLa specific QNX Message Passing end-points are only accessed through LoLa APIs.

items.name: Communication.AragenNotSafe
items.text: Input artifacts shall be manually reviewed for correctness

items.name: Communication.UnsupportedDataTypes
items.text: It shall be ensured that neither variants nor maps are sent via LoLa.

items.name: Communication.NoGuaranteeOnExecutionTime
items.text: There is no guarantee on the execution time of any function call provided by LoLa.

items.name: Communication.UsageOfConfigurationOversubscription
items.text: If event instance "oversubscription" is enabled, LoLa makes no warranty that proxies/consumers can't suffer from data loss! It is the responsibility of the user to adapt scheduling/event-data access in a way that no data-loss happens.

items.name: Communication.SameCompilerSettingsForProviderAndConsumerSide
items.text: All compiler settings having influence on the binary representation of data exchanged via {{mw::com}}/{{LoLa}} (event, field, service-method payloads) have to be identical for compilation of code containing {{mw::com}} proxies and skeletons, which communicate.

items.name: Communication.EventOrFieldReceptionViaGenericProxyNeedsSpecificCare
items.text: When receiving event or field data via untyped {{GenericProxyEvent}} or {{GenericProxyField}}, care has to be taken when accessing the corresponding {{SamplePtr<void>}} delivered by calls to {{GetNewSamples()}}: When casting it to the expected type, it needs to be checked that no access behind the size returned by {{GetSampleSize()}} will happen.

items.name: Communication.CorrectlyConfiguredEventsFieldsPerServiceType
items.text: It shall be ensured that all safety relevant events/fields in the service type are the same in all configurations.

items.name: Communication.NoGuaranteesForTimelyMethodCallExecution
items.text: It shall be ensured that a blocking method call will not harm a safety goal.

items.name: Communication.MethodInArgPtrMatches
items.text: It shall be ensured that the memory locations of the method call in-arguments provided at the caller side are exactly the same as the memory locations as used at the callee side.

items.name: Communication.NoGuaranteeOnSubscriptionStateCorrectness
items.text: For safety critical use cases, an application must treat a SubscriptionState of kSubscribed or kSubscriptionPending (returned by GetSubscriptionState() or reported by the SubscriptionStateChangeHandler) as the same.
